limitations: Independent truth poses are100Hz; body velocity/yaw rate use centred differences, so protection timing has callback/diagnostic resolution.
Requested command, governed NMPC reference and independent true velocity are separately reported. A high requested target does not establish that the governed reference or robot reached it.
A failed/short attempt has no steady_last2s result. Its peak or0.5s mean is descriptive, not a completed steady acceptance.
Geometric foot clearance uses joint FK plus independent truth base pose; no measured foot-contact force is available.
No torque warning alone proves calibrated hardware motor/current compliance. No hardware motion was exercised.

limitations: Previous demonstration used one continuous six-direction sequence; this test starts each direction in a fresh world. These are not paired identical-initial-state causal comparisons.

Forward and backward failed before20s; failure-tail velocities are descriptive and never count as completed steady-state acceptance. Their first motor threshold events precede test abort, and pre-protection height is separated from subsequent height loss.
Passing only one20s trial does not establish repeatability, endurance, hardware torque compliance or real-time deadlines. No physical robot was commanded.

The test-only horizontal overspeed guard was changed1→2m/s to allow the1m/s request; command settle wait3→6s accommodates unchanged acceleration limits. Original relative tracking/wrong-way formulas scale their effective thresholds with command magnitude; all changes are explicit above.

Initial five camera attempts had compatibility/serialization failures, preserved in media metadata. All physical direction results rely on independent telemetry and finalized sweep reports. The final yaw-negative capture succeeded and supplies the shown footage. Capture helper changed between attempts; controller/model/task/binaries remained unchanged.
